mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the effect reverses in a high-inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with falling housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months, combined with falling industrial production (INDPRO), indicates a deteriorating labor market and reduced economic activity, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO declines for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 6% year-over-year while the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals insufficient monetary tightening to contain inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 400k per month for two consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding rise in average hourly earnings, signals labor market expansion without wage inflation, which supports corporate margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 400000 for 2 consecutive months AND no concurrent rise in AHE (not directly observed, but implied by absence of wage inflation proxy)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 3% month-over-month (seasonally adjusted) signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate sales and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise > 3% MoM (SA) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is held constant for four consecutive months amid rising inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%), it signals policy lag or ineffectiveness, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to expectations of future tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.
